clue.text: Call out cooking instructions, but swap pepper for final pinch of salt

indicators.note: swap ... for asks us to take one letter out of the recipe word and put another in its place

parts.note: a recipe is a set of cooking instructions
P stands for pepper, as on a cruet labelled S and P

indicators.note: the final pinch of a word is just its last letter

explanation.surface: A cook tweaks a recipe, replacing the pepper with a little extra salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swap ... for' puts T, the 'final pinch of' salt, where the P of RECIPE was.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory, as when calling out a list to an audience.

clue.text: Some ombre trousers with an old-school look

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Trousers shaded light to dark give a vintage style.
explanation.walkthrough: Ombre is a fabric that fades from one colour to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a style deliberately imitating fashions of the past.

clue.text: Soup, food and wine possibly served up

parts.note: chow is slang for food

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the wine word is written bottom to top

parts.note: red is one kind of wine

explanation.surface: A menu offers soup, a meal and perhaps some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, often of fish or clams.

clue.text: Launches an attack on one artist when drunk

indicators.note: drunk signals the letters of the words before reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter turns aggressive after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear into someone is to attack them fiercely, physically or verbally.

clue.text: Wild fellow that is about to take cocaine

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is

indicators.note: to take means one piece swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived for about, concerning
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A man described as wild is about to use drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce and wild are synonyms describing a savage, untamed animal or temper.

clue.text: It can top a cake if cream is no good at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the words in that run

explanation.surface: A baker's advice: use this topping if the cream has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the initials of 'if cream is no good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread over the top of a cake.

clue.text: Frenchman without a wife left for a fresh start

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the two letters for wife and left surround the a

explanation.surface: A Frenchman whose wife walked out decides on a new beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' puts W and L around A to make WAL after RENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal is a revival or new beginning, much as a fresh start is.

clue.text: Seriously … New Year, let's get smashed!

indicators.note: smashed signals the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A New Year's Eve cry to go out and get very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get smashed' rearranges N with YEAR and LETS. 'Seriously' sounds like sarcasm in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means in a serious, sincere way.

clue.text: Supportive tissue ordered mainly at the front in layers

indicators.note: in places those two opening letters inside the word for layers

parts.note: strata are layers, as of rock

indicators.note: at the front picks the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A description of tissue arranged neatly, largely at the front, in layers.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a stroma is the connective framework of an organ, so stromata are supporting tissues.

clue.text: Ace supplementary dish forming part of a platter?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a side is a side dish served alongside a main

explanation.surface: An excellent side dish served as part of a plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: A platter is old slang for a vinyl record, which has an A and a B side.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-side of a record is the main track, one face of the disc.

clue.text: Region redeveloped to create bypass

indicators.note: redeveloped says the letters of the word before are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A town region is rebuilt to make room for a bypass road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeveloped' rearranges REGION. 'Bypass' looks like a road, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to pass it over or take no notice of it, to disregard it.

clue.text: Work set-up in which, ultimately, kids get on terribly

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word it is attached to
terribly signals the words before are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An office arrangement in which, in the end, children behave badly together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives H from which; 'terribly' rearranges KIDS GET ON into OTDESKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-desking is an office arrangement where workers take any free desk rather than owning one.

clue.text: Went to do some gardening

definitions.meaning: went in the sense of having passed water, the past tense of the childish verb wee
to pull unwanted plants from a flower bed

explanation.surface: Someone headed off to spend time in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is not travel: it is the past tense of wee, to urinate, written WEE'D.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a childish past tense for urinating; the other is clearing garden beds of unwanted plants.

clue.text: Russian leader uncovered a lethal compound

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer covering letters at each end are stripped off

parts.note: a tsarina was an empress, a female ruler of Russia

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler is exposed as owning a deadly chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips T and A from TSARINA, and 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarin is a nerve agent, a deadly chemical weapon.

clue.text: Very chilled character interrupts lecture

indicators.note: interrupts means the character word breaks into the middle of the lecture word

parts.note: to scold is to lecture someone angrily
tone is the character or quality of something

explanation.surface: A cool individual breaks in on a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-cold describes something entirely cold, such as a drink or a dish.

clue.text: Step up key piece of activity after usual close of business?

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: piece of here takes just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: something after the usual end of the working day is late

explanation.surface: An office worker presses a key and does some work after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to intensify or increase something, the same as stepping it up.

clue.text: Jovial politician with six bottles, almost finished

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative politician
VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: almost finished means the last letter is dropped so the word stops short

parts.note: vials are small bottles

explanation.surface: A cheery MP with half a dozen bottles that are nearly empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost finished' cuts the S from VIALS. 'Finished' looks like drained bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Convivial means friendly, lively and fond of good company, like jovial.

clue.text: Family member drops in twice to get some grains

indicators.note: twice says the shortened word is written two times
drops means letters are let fall from the relative's word

parts.note: a cousin is a relative, a family member

explanation.surface: A relative calls round twice to collect some cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes IN from COUSIN to leave COUS; 'twice' doubles it. 'Drops in' looks like visiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is small granules of semolina wheat, cooked as a grain dish.

clue.text: Nearly all poly bags recycled for food in Italy

indicators.note: recycled means the letters are reprocessed into a new arrangement
nearly all means one letter is taken from the end of the first word

explanation.surface: Plastic bags get recycled into Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' cuts Y from poly; 'recycled' rearranges POL with BAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spag bol is British slang for spaghetti bolognese, an Italian pasta dish.

clue.text: No, that was a mistake to turn over and lie front to back!

indicators.note: to turn over means the whole run is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: oops is what you say on making a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone corrects themselves and decides to roll over in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' turns N + OOPS around.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is to lie nestled behind a partner, front to back, like stacked cutlery.

clue.text: Fine, independent newspaper housed in US city

indicators.note: housed in says the letters are lodged inside the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York
the FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A British paper finds a fine new home in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is informal for neat, clever or very good, as in fine.

clue.text: It's just pleasing to start parties

indicators.note: to start places the pleasing word at the front of the charade

parts.note: fair can mean pleasing to the eye, attractive
dos are parties, as in a big do

explanation.surface: It's simply nice to kick things off with parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair do's is British slang for 'that's fair enough', conceding something is just.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment picked up for testing

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so we want a word that sounds like the utensil

parts.note: a beater, such as an egg whisk, is kitchen equipment

explanation.surface: Kitchen utensils are collected so they can be tried out.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without a sounded R, BEATER sounds like BETA.
explanation.definitionFit: A beta version of software is the release put out for trials by users.

clue.text: Food guidelines

definitions.meaning: supplies of food and drink laid in
clauses or stipulations in a contract or law

explanation.surface: A heading for dietary advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisions are stocks of food; provisions are also conditions laid down in an agreement.

clue.text: Looks to make friends

definitions.meaning: slang for one's friends or people

explanation.surface: Appearance is how to make friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeps are quick looks; peeps is also slang for one's pals.

clue.text: Straight away? Yes, or never!

parts.note: now means immediately, straight away
ay is an old or dialect yes, as in a parliamentary vote

explanation.surface: A demand for an immediate answer, yes or no.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No way!' is an emphatic refusal, meaning it will never happen.

clue.text: Revised deal with leaders from Brussels obviously can be made

indicators.note: revised means the letters are reworked into a fresh order
leaders from takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A renegotiated deal, backed by EU chiefs, is clearly achievable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders from' gives B and O; 'Revised' shuffles them with DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doable is achievable, possible to carry out or accomplish.

clue.text: Make final catch in a low position

parts.note: to nail a culprit is to catch them
down means in a lower place

explanation.surface: A fielder makes the last catch while crouched low.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something down is to settle or fix it, making an agreement definite.

clue.text: Food shop's healthy starter is yummy

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop; with 's it is deli's

indicators.note: starter is the opening letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: A deli's healthy first course turns out to be delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' gives H from healthy, after DELI'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Delish is a slangy shortening of delicious, meaning tasty.

clue.text: Wicked phrase — one that indicates agreement

parts.note: ill can mean evil or wicked, as in ill deeds
to phrase something is to say it

explanation.surface: A naughty expression that signals someone is in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'I'll say!' is an emphatic way of agreeing, like 'absolutely'.
